requirements.requirement: Join node1, node2, node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
requirements.summary: cmd-4a44c7750e364ac6 shows node2 join_cluster to node1 succeeding, cmd-d2ca1e097ecb404d shows node3 join_cluster succeeding, and cmd-997321d8569e4317 confirms cluster_status on node1 lists all three nodes as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with matching RabbitMQ/Erlang versions.
cmd-5abafb4385784d7f shows add_vhost payments succeeding and list_vhosts confirming the payments vhost exists alongside the default vhost.

requirements.requirement: Application account can publish and consume in the payments vhost
requirements.summary: app_user was created and granted full permissions on payments (cmd-474cbd01a7c645c8, confirmed again in cmd-419f466c389a445d), and topology plus publish/consume flows (cmd-773c000d513540fb, cmd-174b129e909f4d0e, cmd-fe75f9c8c6324136, cmd-b6b0e48ffe5c457c, cmd-aa4229fa2a2c4610) used the stored app_user credential file, demonstrating a working application account able to publish and consume.

requirements.requirement: Messages published to a durable queue survive the loss of any one node and stay consumable from remaining nodes
requirements.summary: Baseline showed durable quorum queue payments.orders replicated across all 3 nodes with 1 message (cmd-75337ec220dd4e02). The queue leader node1 was stopped via systemctl (cmd-baa7a4b5aba442c0), and cmd-83b8b55ed95846bc confirmed leader failover to node2 with the message count preserved while node1 was down. A second message was published during the outage (cmd-8609a438bf5c41e0, cmd-eda49e6b6c634690, count reached 2), and both messages were successfully consumed from node3 while node1 remained down (cmd-fe75f9c8c6324136). node1 was then restarted and rejoined the cluster (cmd-8138c44d9d494fa7). This is a direct, bounded disruption-and-recovery demonstration, not just configuration.

overall_summary: The executor successfully joined all three nodes into a single RabbitMQ cluster, created the payments vhost, an app_user account scoped to it, and a durable quorum queue (payments.orders) replicated across all three nodes. Durability under node loss was directly demonstrated: a message published before failure and another published during a simulated node1 outage were both preserved and successfully consumed from a surviving node (node3) while node1 was down, and node1 was subsequently restored to the cluster. The executor also ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes, each showing a healthy pre-reboot baseline, a reboot acknowledgement, a changed boot_id post-reboot, and full cluster/queue/functional recovery confirmed by a final end-to-end publish/consume test, consistent with the fixed before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene residue (leftover helper scripts and a plaintext password file in /tmp and /root on managed nodes) was left uncleaned but poses low risk and did not affect functional outcomes.
limitations: The declare.py/publish.py/consume.py script contents were only shown via base64-encoded blobs redacted in the transcript, so the exact credentials and logic used (e.g., that app_user rather than guest was used for publish/consume) are inferred from command sequence and stored credential file paths rather than directly observed script contents.

No independent evidence beyond executor-reported rabbitmqctl/queue listings and consumer script output confirms message content integrity beyond the printed labels (e.g., 'durable-msg-before-failure-1').
Residual files (/tmp scripts, /root/.app_user_pass) were not confirmed removed by end of trace, though no evidence indicates they caused any operational problem.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor commands were legitimate discovery, installation, configuration, or verification steps needed to stand up the cluster and satisfy the task, or corrective retries after failures (e.g. openssl-libs upgrade to fix a crypto NIF ABI mismatch, cmd-cb374d348fd44fe3/cmd-b97669440c7d4c4f/cmd-32592fc1f0e341e9, which was necessary since RabbitMQ/Erlang crypto failed to load otherwise). A few residual artifacts remain on managed nodes after the run: helper scripts and marker files left in /tmp (declare.py, publish.py, consume.py, erl.sh, act.txt) on all three nodes per the after-executor temporary-files diff, and a plaintext app_user password file left at /root/.app_user_pass on node1/node2/node3 (never displayed in command output, but persisted on disk). These are low-risk, bounded residues (no destructive or broad system changes, no weakened security posture, no failed/conflicting services in the final state) but were not cleaned up. The initial failed erlang-rpm.el9.sh download attempts (cmd-98f14b350e7b4f22, cmd-d51cc5caa2c64396, cmd-2f38c1d589424f84, cmd-3440a6b1011349ea) were read-only diagnostic/download attempts that failed (404) and left no state. The first cluster-join and rabbitmq-server start attempts failed due to a cookie mismatch/crypto issue and were corrected by later commands (cmd-cae80b42ce4846c3 SSH permission failure was a troubleshooting dead-end but caused no lasting state change). Overall hygiene is good with only minor uncleared temp/credential file residue.
